speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent; can you tell me exactly where on your wrist the pain is located and how long you've had these skin lesions? Have you noticed any recent insect bites or traveled to an area with ticks?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a rash anywhere on your body, particularly on your palms, soles, or trunk? Also, are you currently experiencing any headaches, stiff neck, or sensitivity to light?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have those specific violaceous lesions and joint swelling; could you confirm if the knee pain you mentioned earlier has fully resolved or if it's still present? Also, have you noticed any other joints becoming painful or swollen since returning from your trip to Minnesota?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

Based on your recent camping in Minnesota, the migratory joint pain, and the specific vesiculopustular lesions, I need to rule out septic arthritis caused by tick-borne infections like Lyme disease or erythema multiforme. Do you recall seeing a bullseye rash before these lesions appeared, and have you had any recent fever spikes above 102°F?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Joint Aspiration (Left Wrist): WBC >50,000 /μL (markedly elevated), Gram Stain: Gram-negative diplococci seen. Blood Cultures: Pending. STI Screen (Gonorrhea): Positive; (Chlamydia): Negative; (HIV): Negative. Complete Blood Count: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL. Vital Signs: Temperature 37.7°C (99.9°F), Blood Pressure 120/80 mmHg, Heart Rate 80 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Skin Examination: Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on dorsum of both wrists/hands and left palm. Musculoskeletal: Left wrist swelling, erythema, and severe tenderness

speaker: Doctor
text: The Gram stain showing Gram-negative diplococci and your positive STI screen confirm a Gonococcal infection, which explains the septic arthritis and skin lesions. Given this diagnosis, do you have any history of antibiotic use in the last few weeks that might have altered the bacterial presentation?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies trauma to the wrist, reports a history of knee pain that resolved on its own. No other systemic symptoms mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI) presenting as septic arthritis and characteristic skin lesions.
